content.text: Perfect! The documentation confirms the issue. According to the search results, when a service is in a different namespace, the pod needs to use the fully qualified DNS name. Let me update the ticket with my findings:

input.note:
**Root Cause:** The notification-worker is configured with `SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay`, but the smtp-relay service was moved from the notify namespace to the shared-infra namespace on Sunday. When a service moves to a different namespace, pods must use the fully qualified DNS name to reach it.

**Evidence:** Pod logs show the DNS lookup failures: "lookup smtp-relay on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host". The pod configuration shows `SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay` (unqualified name), which only works if the service is in the same namespace.

**Fix:** Update the notification-worker configuration to use the fully qualified service name: `SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay.shared-infra` (or `SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay.shared-infra.svc.cluster.local` for full FQDN). According to Kubernetes DNS discovery, "Pods in other namespaces must qualify the name as `my-service.my-ns`" [cite: concepts/services-networking/service#dns-0], and "DNS queries that don't specify a namespace are limited to the pod's namespace. If the namespace of the pod and service differ, the DNS query must include the namespace of the service" [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/dns-debugging-resolution#are-you-in-the-right-namespace-for-the-service-0].
